newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hoyts on target for full year result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hoyts on target for full year result.

text.p: Cinema operator Hoyts Cinemas Ltd said on Wednesday that early trading in the second half of the year to June 30, 1997 indicated Hoyts was in an excellent position to at least meet its prospectus forecast for the year.
In its prospectus, Hoyts forecast a A$22 million net profit for the year to June 30, 1997.

"On the basis of advance statistics from movies to be released in the second half year such as "Jerry Maguire", "Evita", "Batman and Robin", the "Star Wars Trilogy", and the sequel to "Jurassic Park", we believe that, barring unforseen circumstances, we are in an excellent position to at least meet our prospectus forecast for the 12 month period to June 30, 1997," Hoyts chief executive Peter Ivany said in Hoyts' first half results statement.

Earlier on Wednesday, Hoyts reported a A$12.17 million net profit for the six months to January 2, with earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rising 15 percent to A$43.8 million.
The results include a pre-tax profit of A$2.7 million from the sale of the group's stand-alone cinema in Parramatta, in Sydney's western suburbs.

"The results are pleasing and in line with our prospectus forecast," Ivany said. "As indicated in the prospectus we expect to declare an interim dividend of four cents in July 1997 and a final four cent dividend in November 1997," he said.
The strong first half performance of Hoyts' Australian cinemas was expected to be matched in the second half year, Hoyts said.
It said it expected to develop or buy an extra 50 new screens in New South Wales, Victoria, Western Australia and in New Zealand by the end of 1997.
Hoyts, however, said the performance from its U.S. operations was lower than expected in the first half because of weaker films and the Olympic games.
"The impact of slower box office admissions during the period affected all exhibitors," it said.
It said it planned to develop or buy an extra 132 screens in North Eastern United States by the end of 1997, having already bought 93 screens in the area in the first half.
These extra screens would be reflected in improved second half earnings from the United States.
"Box office admissions have improved significantly in the U.S. since the latter part of January 1997 as a solid line-up of film releases commences," it said.
"We believe that the product to be released in the second half will compensate for the relatively poor product in the first half," Ivany said.
Hoyts' shares were down two cents at A$2.66 at 12.20 (0120 GMT).
